quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding in a group, what is the best way to stay close together while keeping safe distance?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets riders stay close while keeping a safe distance from each other. Use a single-file line when turning, curving, or entering or leaving a highway. Never ride side-by-side with another rider.

questions.question: What can goggles protect?

options.text: Your face but not your eyes.
Your eyes, but not your face.
Neither your face nor your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your eyes, but not your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes. Only a face shield can protect your entire face in a crash.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up, as this makes the wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can. Avoid braking, as this can also make the wobble worse.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight. Wearing bright colors and reflective materials at all times makes you more visible and safer.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, where should you look?

options.text: Close to the front of the motorcycle.
Through the turn to where you want to go.
Turn your entire body to see through the turn.
Increase your speed before the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Through the turn to where you want to go.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn just your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger in a sidecar, what should you do?

options.text: Brake harder than usual to stop quickly.
Brake more softly than usual to save the brakes.

questions.explanation: The extra weight of a sidecar passenger changes how your motorcycle handles. Your motorcycle will need more space to stop completely.

questions.question: How should a group of riders pass another vehicle?
questions.explanation: On a two-lane highway, riders should pass one at a time. The second rider waits until the first rider has safely returned to the original lane before passing. Continue this pattern until all riders have safely passed.

questions.question: Which type of sign is rectangular?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, like speed limit signs, are rectangular. They are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road hazards or conditions.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
questions.explanation: BAC is affected by how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Height does not affect BAC.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help a rider become more visible?
questions.explanation: To be visible, wear bright clothing with reflective materials, use your headlight at all times, and use your turn signals and brake light correctly.

questions.question: If road conditions require a longer stopping distance, you should:

options.text: Let someone else ride your motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs more time to stop. This includes slippery pavement, poor visibility, or heavy traffic. Use at least a three-second following distance.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Avoid using your high beam headlight.

questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distances at night. Slow down and increase your following distance. Use your high beam whenever you are not meeting or following another vehicle.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance:

options.text: If there are only a few vehicles on the road.
If drivers are following the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs more time to stop. This includes slippery pavement, poor visibility, or heavy traffic where another driver might cut in front of you.

questions.question: A person with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of ______ or higher is considered legally intoxicated.
questions.explanation: If you are 21 or older and riding a motorcycle with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher, you are legally intoxicated. Riding while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Sit as far back on the bike as possible.

questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean when the operator leans. Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the operator and hold onto their waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, the best action is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If you can do so safely, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may only encourage them to tailgate faster.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes:

options.text: Involve riders with less than six months of experience.
Are caused by faulty ignition systems.
Occur because of distractions from passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with less than six months of experience.
questions.explanation: Be very careful when riding a new motorcycle. Most motorcycle crashes involve riders who have less than six months of experience on that particular motorcycle.

questions.question: When downshifting, you should:

options.text: Shift through multiple gears at once.
Shift through one gear at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift through one gear at a time.
questions.explanation: When shifting to a lower gear, shift down one gear at a time. Gradually release the clutch between each downshift.

questions.question: Riders without helmets are ________ to die in a crash than riders with helmets.
questions.explanation: At any speed, riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets.

questions.question: What is the best protection when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Keep distance between your motorcycle and other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep distance between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid crashes is to keep space between you and other vehicles. This gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. Wearing proper safety gear is also important.

questions.question: What does a face shield do?

options.text: Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic face shield that resists impact gives the best protection for your eyes and face. Regular eyeglasses or sunglasses are not enough. In Vermont, you don't need eye or face protection if your motorcycle has a windshield, but it is still recommended.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's braking power comes from the front brake?
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What helmet gives you the most protection?

options.text: A helmet that meets U.S. DOT standards.
A helmet that has been in a previous crash.
A helmet that provides hearing protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: A helmet that meets U.S. DOT standards.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. Helmets should fit snugly all the way around your head.

questions.question: When riding at night, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Use your high beam light when possible.

questions.explanation: When riding at night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance to avoid crashes. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead of you to see the road better. Use your high beam headlight, except when following or meeting another vehicle.
